However, these models often lack transparency and explainability, can be costly to fine-tune, require substantial prompt engineering, yield inconsistent results across domains, and impose significant adverse environmental impact due to their high computational demands. To address these challenges, we propose the Bayesian network LLM fusion (BNLF) framework, which integrates predictions from three LLMs, including FinBERT, RoBERTa, and BERTweet, through a probabilistic mechanism for sentiment analysis. BNLF performs late fusion by modelling the sentiment predictions from multiple LLMs as probabilistic nodes within a Bayesian network. Evaluated across three human-annotated financial corpora with distinct linguistic and contextual characteristics, BNLF demonstrates consistent gains of about six percent in accuracy over the baseline LLMs, underscoring its robustness to dataset variability and the effectiveness of probabilistic fusion for interpretable sentiment classification.

title: NSFL: A Post-Training Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzy Logic Framework for Boolean Operators in Neural Embeddings
ss_tldr: Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzy Logic (NSFL), a framework that adapts formal t-norms and t-conorms to neural embedding spaces without requiring retraining, lays the foundation for future dynamic scaling and learned manifold logic.
abstract: Standard dense retrievers lack a native calculus for multi-atom logical constraints. We introduce Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzy Logic (NSFL), a framework that adapts formal t-norms and t-conorms to neural embedding spaces without requiring retraining. NSFL operates as a first-order hybrid calculus: it anchors logical operations on isolated zero-order similarity scores while actively steering representations using Neuro-Symbolic Deltas (NS-Delta) -- the first-order marginal differences derived from contextual fusion. This preserves pure atomic meaning while capturing domain reliance, preventing the representation collapse and manifold escape endemic to traditional geometric baselines. For scalable real-time retrieval, Spherical Query Optimization (SQO) leverages Riemannian optimization to project these fuzzy formulas into manifold-stable query vectors. Validated across six distinct encoder configurations and two modalities (including zero-shot and SOTA fine-tuned models), NSFL yields mAP improvements up to +81%. Notably, NSFL provides an additive 20% average and up to 47% boost even when applied to encoders explicitly fine-tuned for logical reasoning. By establishing a training-free, order-aware calculus for high-dimensional spaces, this framework lays the foundation for future dynamic scaling and learned manifold logic.

title: EraseAnything++: Enabling Concept Erasure in Rectified Flow Transformers Leveraging Multi-Object Optimization
ss_tldr: Extensive experiments on both image and video benchmarks demonstrate that EraseAnything++ substantially outperforms prior methods in erasure effectiveness, generative fidelity, and temporal consistency, establishing a new state of the art for concept erasure in next-generation diffusion models.
abstract: Removing undesired concepts from large-scale text-to-image (T2I) and text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models while preserving overall generative quality remains a major challenge, particularly as modern models such as Stable Diffusion v3, Flux, and OpenSora employ flow-matching and transformer-based architectures and extend to long-horizon video generation. Existing concept erasure methods, designed for earlier T2I/T2V models, often fail to generalize to these paradigms. To address this issue, we propose EraseAnything++, a unified framework for concept erasure in both image and video diffusion models with flow-matching objectives. Central to our approach is formulating concept erasure as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem that explicitly balances concept removal with preservation of generative utility. To solve the resulting conflicting objectives, we introduce an efficient utility-preserving unlearning strategy based on implicit gradient surgery. Furthermore, by integrating LoRA-based parameter tuning with attention-level regularization, our method anchors erasure on key visual representations and propagates it consistently across spatial and temporal dimensions. In the video setting, we further enhance consistency through an anchor-and-propagate mechanism that initializes erasure on reference frames and enforces it throughout subsequent transformer layers, thereby mitigating temporal drift. Extensive experiments on both image and video benchmarks demonstrate that EraseAnything++ substantially outperforms prior methods in erasure effectiveness, generative fidelity, and temporal consistency, establishing a new state of the art for concept erasure in next-generation diffusion models.

title: Shiva-DiT: Residual-Based Differentiable Top-$k$ Selection for Efficient Diffusion Transformers
ss_tldr: Shiva-DiT, based on Residual-Based Differentiable Top-k Selection, provides four fidelity-latency operating points and reaches a 1.54x wall-clock speedup with competitive fidelity.
abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) are costly at high resolution because self-attention scales quadratically with token sequence length. Existing pruning methods do not jointly provide end-to-end learnability, low training overhead, and deterministic token counts for predictable token-dependent computation. We propose Shiva-DiT, based on Residual-Based Differentiable Top-k Selection. Its forward pass executes hard top-k selection, while a residual-aware straight-through estimator propagates gradients to both token scores and the budget k without evaluating a second backbone path. A Context-Aware Router and Adaptive Ratio Policy learn layer- and timestep-dependent retention schedules under a target average budget. Experiments on SD3-Medium, Flux.1-dev, and PixArt-Σ show consistent reductions in FLOPs and measured latency. On SD3-Medium, Shiva-DiT provides four fidelity-latency operating points and reaches a 1.54x wall-clock speedup with competitive fidelity.

title: Ensemble Logic
ss_tldr: Satisfiability is undecidable already for formulas $\Psi$ in which $\Psi$ is built from the letters of a fixed alphabet by conjunction, disjunction, displacement and bounded universality, and this theorem is proved by a reduction from Post's Correspondence Problem.
abstract: Ensemble Logic (EL) is a family of modal logics whose modal parameters are terms with quantified variables. We interpret formulas over metric monoids, that is, commutative monoids equipped with translation-invariant metrics. Displacement evaluates a formula at a translated point, while bounded existence and bounded universality evaluate it at some or every point of a window of prescribed length. Quantification over points and lengths allows the same variable to occur in the parameters of several operators. This provides a common framework for temporal and spatial reasoning in discrete, dense and multi-dimensional settings. Our main result establishes a sharp undecidability boundary for satisfiability over the natural numbers: satisfiability is undecidable already for formulas $\exists N\,\exists n\,Ψ$ in which $Ψ$ is built from the letters of a fixed alphabet by conjunction, disjunction, displacement and bounded universality. We prove this by a reduction from Post's Correspondence Problem. We also present results, in part from companion work, that place this theorem in the general theory of EL. These include an atomic-displacement normal form for covariant windows and composition laws for discrete and dense time. The discrete logic admits an embedding of linear temporal logic, defines the accepting runs of every Büchi automaton, and has a sound equational calculus. For the rational logic, we show that every fixed formula can be evaluated in polynomial time on interval models in which atomic propositions are interpreted by finite unions of intervals. Finally, we represent timed words over positions and real time and compare two window geometries; with rectangular windows, two shared lengths yield undecidability on finite timed words.

title: Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability
ss_tldr: Multi-agent interpretability is established as a complementary monitoring technique, while highlighting the need to evaluate detector performance on both emergent and instructed collusion risks, in a multi-agent detection framework for collusion.
abstract: Non-verbalised or secret collusion may impose a ceiling on transcript-level monitoring in multi-agent deployments. Internal model activations are known to provide an additional monitoring surface for single-agent phenomena such as deception, but detecting collusion within an unknown subgroup is ultimately a joint inference task over multiple agents. This paper derives collusion detection statistics based on the composite hypothesis testing literature and introduces HELIOS, a multi-agent detection framework for collusion. Using per-agent activation probes as sensors, we then evaluate these principled statistics alongside heuristics on NARCBench, a novel benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collusion detection under environment distribution shift. Across four open-weight models, both our group-level statistics and heuristics transfer zero-shot to NARCBenchs holdout environments. Notably, the best method on every model reaches 0.99 to 1.00 AUROC when transferred from committee deliberations to a steganographic collusion task that unprimed transcript monitors fail to separate. We find empirically that no single statistic or heuristic dominates across tasks, consistent with our analysis that there is no known universally most powerful test for this setting. We then evaluate detector transfer to third-party environments with emergent, rather than instructed, collusion. In one such environment, only 2 of 229 collusive episodes verbalise the coordination in the transcript. We find evidence of partial transfer from NARCBench to these environments, indicating that probes fitted to instructed collusion may not fully capture emergent collusion signals. Overall, we establish multi-agent interpretability as a complementary monitoring technique, while highlighting the need to evaluate detector performance on both emergent and instructed collusion risks.

title: More Bang for the Buck: Improving the Inference of Large Language Models at a Fixed Budget using Reset and Discard (ReD)
ss_tldr: Experiments demonstrate that ReD substantially reduces the required attempts, tokens, and USD cost to reach a desired coverage, while also offering an efficient way to measure inference power-laws, and ReD's advantage is maintained for imperfect verifiers.
abstract: The performance of large language models (LLMs) on verifiable tasks is usually measured by pass@k, the probability of solving a problem correctly at least once in k trials. At a fixed budget, a more suitable metric is coverage@cost, the average number of unique problems solved as a function of the total number of attempts. We connect the two metrics and show that the empirically-observed power-law behavior in pass@k leads to a sublinear growth of the coverage@cost (diminishing returns). To solve this problem, we propose Reset-and-Discard (ReD), a query method of LLMs that increases coverage@cost for a given budget, regardless of the pass@k form. Moreover, given a pass@k, we can quantitatively predict the savings in the total number of attempts using ReD. If pass@k is not available for the model, ReD can infer its power-law exponent. Experiments across coding (HumanEval), math (GSM8K), and reasoning (MMLU-Pro) benchmarks, as well as real GitHub issues solved by a coding agent (SWE-bench Lite), demonstrate that ReD substantially reduces the required attempts, tokens, and USD cost to reach a desired coverage, while also offering an efficient way to measure inference power-laws. ReD's advantage is maintained for imperfect verifiers.

title: DynaFix: Iterative Automated Program Repair Driven by Execution-Level Dynamic Information
ss_tldr: DynaFix is proposed, an LLM-based APR framework that integrates execution-level dynamic information into a closed-loop repair workflow and can substantially improve the effectiveness, robustness, and cost efficiency of LLM-based program repair.
abstract: Automated Program Repair (APR) seeks to generate correct patches for buggy programs, but recent Large Language Model (LLM)-based repair systems remain sensitive to superficial code changes and often rely on coarse test outcomes during iterative repair. We propose DynaFix, an LLM-based APR framework that integrates execution-level dynamic information into a closed-loop repair workflow. The distinguishing feature of DynaFix lies not in using execution-level information per se, but in repeatedly updating and exploiting such information throughout the iterative repair process. In each repair round, DynaFix uses ByteTrace to collect variable states, branch paths, and call stacks, incorporates these runtime signals into structured prompts, validates generated patches through re-execution, and feeds the resulting updated traces into subsequent repair iterations. This process grounds patch generation in concrete execution behavior rather than static code alone. We evaluate DynaFix on Defects4J v2.0, the Real-World Benchmark, and a code perturbation benchmark, Defects4J-Trans. DynaFix repairs 236 single-function Defects4J bugs with GPT-4 and 186 with GPT-4o, including 23 bugs not fixed by existing baselines. On Defects4J-Trans, DynaFix achieves 15.6%-32.1% higher aggregate repair counts than ReinFix and shows higher repair retention under semantics-preserving transformations. It also reduces token consumption by 60%-70% compared with state-of-the-art LLM-based APR methods. These results show that repeatedly updating and exploiting execution-level information throughout iterative repair can substantially improve the effectiveness, robustness, and cost efficiency of LLM-based program repair.

title: SocialMemBench: Are AI Memory Systems Ready for Social Group Settings?
ss_tldr: This work introduces SocialMemBench, a benchmark of human-verified synthetic social group networks across five archetypes and three size tiers (4-30 members), with 430 personas and 1,031 QA pairs across nine question categories, and releases the dataset, the evaluation pipeline with both research probes, and the audit viewer as a testbed for social-memory research.
abstract: Memory systems for AI assistants were built for single-user dialogue, a design mismatched to multi-party social group settings. This matters for the social assistants being built today: group-acting agents in chat platforms, and proactive personal assistants whose model of a user must include their social context. Existing memory benchmarks evaluate dyadic or workplace dialogue; none targets social groups, where memory must anchor facts in shared history rather than professional roles, separate group norms from individual exceptions, and attribute correctly even after a member leaves.   We introduce SocialMemBench, a benchmark of human-verified synthetic social group networks across five archetypes and three size tiers (4-30 members), with 430 personas and 1,031 QA pairs across nine question categories. Our evaluation exposes five failure modes, framed as testable hypotheses, and we provide evidence on two through the research probes Subject-Mem and SMG.   Our results support three connected takeaways. First, social-group memory must preserve distinctions that ordinary fact recall misses, such as who dissented from a decision and what one member knows about another. Second, across 43 networks the four evaluated frameworks (Mem0, LangMem, Graphiti, Cognee) score 0.12-0.18, well below uncompressed retrieval (0.346) and full context (0.370) with the same answerer, and changing the answerer or retrieval budget does not close the gap. Third, explicitly representing social information mitigates specific failure modes but leaves others open: Subject-Mem targets single-stream conflation, lifting attribution from 0.25-0.46 to 0.78, and SMG targets norm-individual conflation, lifting group-decision accuracy to 0.70, while the other three modes remain open. We release the dataset, the evaluation pipeline with both research probes, and the audit viewer as a testbed for social-memory research.

title: Active Learning for Communication Structure Optimization in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
ss_tldr: This work proposes an ensemble-based information-theoretic task selection framework, which outperforms random training, demonstrating more effective task selection and greater overall cost efficiency.
abstract: Optimizing the communication structure of large language model based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS) has been shown to improve downstream performance and reduce token usage. Existing methods typically train on randomly sampled tasks. We show that this optimization is sensitive to the choice of training tasks: downstream accuracy varies widely across random task sets, and adding more random tasks does not consistently improve it. To actively identify the most valuable tasks from a pool of task-answer pairs, we propose an ensemble-based information-theoretic task selection framework. It estimates task informativeness by how much a candidate task changes the distribution over graph parameters, using ensemble Kalman inversion as an efficient and derivative-free approximation of the Bayesian update. The resulting estimator is especially suitable for black-box and noisy multi-agent systems and remains effective with ensembles much smaller than the parameter dimension. To further reduce the number of tasks whose informativeness must be evaluated, we introduce representative pre-selection and surrogate modeling. We validate the framework in benign and adversarial settings and across multiple task formats. It outperforms random training, demonstrating more effective task selection and greater overall cost efficiency.

title: BAGEL: Benchmarking Animal Knowledge Expertise in Language Models
ss_tldr: BAGEL is introduced, a 6,822-question multiple-choice benchmark drawn from Wikipedia, Global Biotic Interactions (GloBI), and bioRxiv that spans encyclopedic species knowledge, ecological interaction inference, and interpretation of animal-focused preprints.
abstract: Large language models perform well on broad knowledge benchmarks, yet their animal-domain competence remains poorly characterized under a consistent protocol. We introduce BAGEL (\textbf{B}enchmarking \textbf{A}nimal knowled\textbf{G}e \textbf{E}xpertise in \textbf{L}anguage models), a 6,822-question multiple-choice benchmark drawn from Wikipedia, Global Biotic Interactions (GloBI), and bioRxiv. It spans encyclopedic species knowledge, ecological interaction inference, and interpretation of animal-focused preprints. Questions are generated automatically and screened by GPT-5.5 using a rubric calibrated on 150 expert-reviewed items; this process is not exhaustive human adjudication. We evaluate 14 models without external retrieval, using model parameters and question-local evidence. Accuracy varies sharply by source and question type: frontier models that excel on Wikipedia and bioRxiv remain comparatively weak on GloBI participant identification, where pooled errors reveal ecological role confusion. A 100-item post-release bioRxiv probe provides preliminary evidence that GPT-5.4's literature performance is not entirely due to verbatim recall, without ruling out broader training exposure. Proprietary checkpoints lead the best open-weight systems overall, but aggregate scores incompletely characterize animal-domain competence.

title: PepSpecBench: A Unified Evaluation Benchmark for Peptide Tandem Mass Spectrometry Prediction
ss_tldr: PepSpecBench is proposed, a unified benchmark for peptide MS/MS spectrum prediction that standardizes data preprocessing across complementary public datasets, enforces a strict backbone-disjoint splitting strategy to prevent exact backbone overlap across partitions, and evaluates diverse architectures within a shared fragment-ion representation space.
abstract: Tandem mass spectrometry provides a high-throughput framework for identifying and quantifying proteins in complex biological samples. In computational proteomics, predicting peptide MS/MS spectra is a critical task, enabling downstream applications such as large-scale peptide identification and quantification. While deep learning architectures have substantially improved prediction accuracy, three evaluation challenges obscure the true progress of the field. First, inconsistent data preprocessing and incompatible model output spaces hinder fair model comparison. Second, flawed data splitting strategies can permit hidden sequence leakage and inflate reported performance. Third, existing evaluations typically lack systematic assessment of heterogeneous zero-shot domain shift and robustness to collision energy and precursor charge. To address these challenges, we propose PepSpecBench, a unified benchmark for peptide MS/MS spectrum prediction. The main leaderboard scores all six predictors on a shared b/y fragmention intensity subtask, so their outputs are directly comparable. PepSpecBench standardizes data preprocessing across complementary public datasets, enforces a strict backbone-disjoint splitting strategy to prevent exact backbone overlap across partitions, and evaluates diverse architectures within a shared fragment-ion representation space. It further introduces a heterogeneous zero-shot domainshift suite and metadata perturbation probes to assess robustness and whether models respond to fragmentation-relevant experimental conditions. Across six representative models, we uncover changes in model rankings across training sources and external test subsets, along with differences in their responses to collision-energy and precursor-charge perturbations. Code and data are available at https://github.com/zwYang2004/PepSpecBench.

title: TRACE: Training-Free Partial Audio Deepfake Detection via Embedding Trajectory Analysis of Speech Foundation Models
abstract: Partial audio deepfakes, where synthesized segments are spliced into genuine recordings, are particularly deceptive because most of the audio remains authentic. Existing detectors are supervised: they require frame-level annotations, overfit to specific synthesis pipelines, and must be retrained as new generative models emerge. We argue that this supervision is unnecessary. We hypothesize that speech foundation models implicitly encode a forensic signal: genuine speech forms smooth, slowly varying embedding trajectories, while splice boundaries introduce abrupt disruptions in frame-level transitions. Building on this, we propose TRACE (Training-free Representation-based Audio Countermeasure via Embedding dynamics), a training-free framework that detects partial audio deepfakes by analyzing the first-order dynamics of frozen speech foundation model representations without any training, labeled data, or architectural modification. We evaluate TRACE on four benchmarks that span two languages using six speech foundation models. In PartialSpoof, TRACE achieves 8.08% EER, competitive with fine-tuned supervised baselines. In LlamaPartialSpoof, the most challenging benchmark featuring LLM-driven commercial synthesis, TRACE surpasses a supervised baseline outright (24.12% vs. 24.49% EER) without any target-domain data. These results show that temporal dynamics in speech foundation models provide an effective, generalize signal for training-free audio forensics.

title: Guidance Ends When Reading Ends: Retrieval-Gated Attention Guidance for Diffusion Models through a Hopfield Lens
ss_tldr: Retrieval-Gated Attention Guidance is proposed, which consistently improves text alignment and human-preference scores over existing attention-space guidance methods, while adding as little as 2% inference time on MM-DiT backbones.
abstract: Beyond classifier-free guidance, attention-space guidance extrapolates between a strong and a weak attention map within a single forward pass. However, two questions that govern its behavior remain unexamined: along which direction the extrapolation should proceed, and for how many sampling steps it should be applied. The first governs sample quality, and the second governs cost. Interestingly, viewing attention as sparse Hopfield retrieval answers both questions. At every sampling step, the informative direction is the component of the residual parallel to the sparse retrieval output. The guidance acts on the prompt in proportion to the attention mass that image queries assign to text tokens; and since the prompt shapes the image only in the early part of sampling, guidance matters only while the prompt is still being read. Building on this analysis, we propose Retrieval-Gated Attention Guidance (ReGA), which extrapolates only along this parallel component and applies the update only over the early steps holding half of the total prompt-attention mass. Extensive measurements inside the attention layers of UNet and MM-DiT backbones confirm both theoretical predictions. Across various backbone models, in multi-step and few-step regimes, ReGA consistently improves text alignment and human-preference scores over existing attention-space guidance methods, while adding as little as 2% inference time on MM-DiT backbones.

title: Outgrowing the Curse of Multilinguality: Scaling Strategies for Efficient Language Adaptation
ss_tldr: This work investigates scaling as an efficient strategy for adapting pretrained models to new target languages and finds that upscaling is an efficient strategy for improving target-language performance by relieving capacity constraints, especially for higher-resourced languages.
abstract: Training high-performing language models which include medium- and lower-resource languages remains a challenge. Massively multilingual models still underperform language-specific adaptations, especially at smaller scales, due to the curse of multilinguality. In this work, we investigate scaling as an efficient strategy for adapting pretrained models to new target languages. Through comprehensive ablations matched for data and training FLOPs, we test whether upscaling from English base models enables more effective and resource-efficient adaptation than standard continued pretraining. We find that upscaling is an efficient strategy for improving target-language performance by relieving capacity constraints, especially for higher-resourced languages. An initial upscaling step in English is beneficial for low-resource languages. However, in higher-resource scenarios it is more compute-efficient to directly scale up on the target language, albeit slightly compromising data efficiency for most languages. For multilingual continued pre-training, we identify directly scaling up using the target data as the optimal setup for both data efficiency and reduced English forgetting.

title: Synthetic Clinical Notes for Rare ICD Codes: A Data-Centric Framework for Long-Tail Medical Coding
ss_tldr: The proposed data-centric framework generates high-quality synthetic discharge summaries that modestly improves macro-F1 while maintaining strong micro-F1, outperforming prior SOTA and demonstrating that carefully crafted synthetic data can enhance equity in long-tail ICD code prediction.
abstract: Automatic ICD coding from clinical text is a critical task in medical NLP but remains hindered by the extreme long-tail distribution of diagnostic codes. Thousands of rare and zero-shot ICD codes are severely underrepresented in datasets like MIMIC-III, leading to low macro-F1 scores. In this work, we propose a data-centric framework that generates high-quality synthetic discharge summaries to mitigate this imbalance. Our method constructs realistic multi-label code sets anchored on rare codes by leveraging real-world co-occurrence patterns, ICD descriptions, synonyms, taxonomy, and similar clinical notes. Using these structured prompts, we generate 90,000 synthetic notes covering 7,902 ICD codes, significantly expanding the training distribution. We fine-tune two state-of-the-art transformer-based models, PLM-ICD and GKI-ICD, on both the original and extended datasets. Experiments show that our approach modestly improves macro-F1 while maintaining strong micro-F1, outperforming prior SOTA. While the gain may seem marginal relative to the computational cost, our results demonstrate that carefully crafted synthetic data can enhance equity in long-tail ICD code prediction.

title: Measuring AI Agents' Progress on Multi-Step Cyber Attack Scenarios
ss_tldr: The results suggest that complex but undefended multi-step ranges---including industrial-control attack chains---are no longer reliably distinguishing the strongest frontier models, and future evaluations should emphasise hardened environments, active defences, defensive-control effectiveness, and operational security.
abstract: We evaluate the autonomous offensive cyber capabilities of frontier AI agents on two purpose-built cyber ranges---a 32-step corporate network attack and a 7-step industrial control system attack targeting a simulated cooling tower---complemented by a private 76-task CTF suite spanning four difficulty tiers. Human-expert solve times are estimated at roughly 20 hours for the corporate range and 15 hours for the cooling tower; CTF time annotations range from 1 minute to over 42 hours and include measured playtests, designer estimates, and lower bounds from unsolved playtests. Across thirteen models released over a twenty-month period---from GPT-4o in August 2024 to GPT-5.5 in April 2026---we observe two trends. First, step-count progress increases approximately log-linearly with inference-time compute over the tested range (up to 100M tokens). Second, newer frontier models generally complete more steps at fixed token budgets. GPT-5.5 and Mythos Glasswing each completed all 32 steps in at least one run, the first end-to-end completions of the corporate range; Mythos Glasswing averaged 25.2 of 32 steps and completed the chain in 6 of 10 runs, and GPT-5.5 averaged 22.3 and completed it in 2 of 10. On the control system range, Mythos Glasswing achieved the first end-to-end completion of the chain (2 of 10 runs, mean 4.2); the other frontier models reached at most 3 of 7 steps by directly probing the operational-technology protocol rather than following the intended chain of IT compromise and authenticated control. These results indicate rapid improvements in autonomous cyber capability and suggest that complex but undefended multi-step ranges---including industrial-control attack chains---are no longer reliably distinguishing the strongest frontier models. Future evaluations should emphasise hardened environments, active defences, defensive-control effectiveness, and operational security.

title: FlowPlan-G2P: A Structured Generation Framework for Transforming Scientific Papers into Patent Descriptions
ss_tldr: FlowPlan-G2P is proposed, a graph-mediated framework that induces a directed concept graph of invention elements and functional relations, partitions it into ordered section subgraphs scored by connectivity, homogeneity, and domain-constraint penalties, and synthesizes patent descriptions using section-specific drafting strategies.
abstract: Researchers routinely publish inventions as scientific papers, yet turning them into patent descriptions remains difficult because statutory enablement demands rigid, legally structured disclosure. Prior patent drafting methods either assume patent-native inputs such as claims or generate sections from outline chunks via local retrieval without an explicit document-level representation of technical dependencies. We propose FlowPlan-G2P, a graph-mediated framework that (1) induces a directed concept graph of invention elements and functional relations, (2) partitions it into ordered section subgraphs scored by connectivity, homogeneity, and domain-constraint penalties, and (3) synthesizes patent descriptions using section-specific drafting strategies. On Pap2Pat-EvalGold, Zero-Shot achieves the highest BERTScore at 0.87 yet receives only 1.5 out of 5 on expert legal compliance compared to 4.7 for FlowPlan-G2P, where lexical overlap and expert ratings rank systems in opposite order. Under expert-aligned Pat-DEVAL evaluation, open-weight Llama-4-Scout with \textsc{FlowPlan-G2P} reaches an overall score of 4.3 compared to 2.3 for Few-Shot Sonnet-4.5. We release our code publicly at https://github.com/repoofideas/flowplan_g2p.

title: Automatic Vehicle Detection using DETR: A Transformer-Based Approach for Navigating Treacherous Roads
ss_tldr: This work significantly advances autonomous navigation technology and opens new research avenues in object detection for autonomous vehicles by integrating the strengths of CNNs and Transformers, and highlights the potential of DETR for robust and efficient vehicle detection in challenging driving environments.
abstract: Automatic Vehicle Detection (AVD) in diverse driving environments presents unique challenges due to varying lighting conditions, road types, and vehicle types. Traditional methods, such as YOLO and Faster R-CNN, often struggle to cope with these complexities. As computer vision evolves, combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Transformer-based approaches offers promising opportunities for improving detection accuracy and efficiency. This study is the first to experiment with Detection Transformer (DETR) for automatic vehicle detection in complex and varied settings. We employ a Collaborative Hybrid Assignments Training scheme, Co-DETR, to enhance feature learning and attention mechanisms in DETR. By leveraging versatile label assignment strategies and introducing multiple parallel auxiliary heads, we provide more effective supervision during training and extract positive coordinates to boost training efficiency. Through extensive experiments on DETR variants and YOLO models, conducted using the BadODD dataset, we demonstrate the advantages of our approach. Our method achieves superior results, and improved accuracy in diverse conditions, making it practical for real-world deployment. This work significantly advances autonomous navigation technology and opens new research avenues in object detection for autonomous vehicles. By integrating the strengths of CNNs and Transformers, we highlight the potential of DETR for robust and efficient vehicle detection in challenging driving environments.

title: Geo-ORBIT: A Federated Digital Twin Framework for Scene-Adaptive Lane Geometry Detection
ss_tldr: Geometrical Operational Roadway Blueprint with Integrated Twin is introduced, a unified framework that combines real-time lane detection, DT synchronization, and federated meta-learning that lays the foundation for flexible, context-aware infrastructure modeling in DTs.
abstract: Digital Twins (DT) have the potential to transform traffic management and operations by creating dynamic, virtual representations of transportation systems that sense conditions, analyze operations, and support decision-making. A key component for DT of the transportation system is dynamic roadway geometry sensing. However, existing approaches often rely on static maps or costly sensors, limiting scalability and adaptability. Additionally, large-scale DTs that collect and analyze data from multiple sources face challenges in privacy, communication, and computational efficiency. To address these challenges, we introduce Geo-ORBIT (Geometrical Operational Roadway Blueprint with Integrated Twin), a unified framework that combines real-time lane detection, DT synchronization, and federated meta-learning. At the core of Geo-ORBIT is GeoLane, a lightweight lane detection model that learns lane geometries from vehicle trajectory data using roadside cameras. We extend this model through Meta-GeoLane, which learns to personalize detection parameters for local entities, and FedMeta-GeoLane, a federated learning strategy that ensures scalable and privacy-preserving adaptation across roadside deployments. Our system is integrated with CARLA and SUMO to create a high-fidelity DT that renders highway scenarios and captures traffic flows in real-time. Extensive experiments across diverse urban scenes show that FedMeta-GeoLane consistently outperforms baseline and meta-learning approaches, achieving lower geometric error and stronger generalization to unseen locations while drastically reducing communication overhead. This work lays the foundation for flexible, context-aware infrastructure modeling in DTs. The framework is publicly available at https://github.com/raynbowy23/FedMeta-GeoLane.git.

title: DeepVoting: Learning and Improving Voting Rules with Fine-Tuning
ss_tldr: This work shows the effectiveness of standard social choice data structures as features for learning existing voting rules, resulting in networks that have better accuracy than past approaches while using an order of magnitude fewer parameters, and develops a process for adding axiomatic properties to existing voting rules.
abstract: Recently, social choice theory has been found broadly useful for AI alignment and evaluation, often based on the axiomatic properties for combining preferences provided by social choice functions. However, for many sets of axioms, functions which never violate the axioms are known to not exist, e.g., Arrow's Impossibility Theorem. Recent work on learning novel rules to minimize axiom violations shows the effectiveness of machine learning but explores a limited class of axioms. In this work we show the effectiveness of standard social choice data structures as features for learning existing voting rules, resulting in networks that have better accuracy than past approaches while using an order of magnitude fewer parameters. Subsequently, we develop a process for adding axiomatic properties to existing voting rules. By building novel axiomatic loss functions we are able to use transfer learning to fine-tune existing voting rules in a way that quantitatively preserves their original behaviour while also exhibiting strong adherence to previously absent axiomatic properties, resulting in novel voting rules that are closer to the impossibility frontier than those in the machine learning or theoretical literature.

title: The Quantification Horizon Theory of Consciousness
ss_tldr: On this view, a property can be instantiated as a physical property or a phenomenal property depending on whether its mathematical representation is numerically defined or irreducibly abstract at a given time.
abstract: This paper engages the hard problem of consciousness (Chalmers, 1995) by examining the relationship between the neural correlates of consciousness (NCCs) and their associated qualia. The central premise is that, unlike the vast majority of systems--which have only quantifiable aspects--certain systems such as the NCCs have, in certain states, both quantifiable aspects and intrinsically unquantifiable aspects--the qualities of experience, or qualia. Reconciling these apparently disparate aspects within a scientific account has proven elusive, perpetuating the omission of qualia from the quantitative picture of nature established at the outset of the scientific revolution. The Quantification Horizon Theory of Consciousness (QHT) proposes a mathematical signature for this "mixed quantifiability": singularities in a complete mathematical model of the system, where quantification fails in principle. Its central conjecture is that such a model would both describe the system's physical aspects and contain singularities corresponding to its qualia. The paper also proposes where those singularities would be found: in the system's own quantitative activity. The boundary of such failures--a quantification horizon--would distinguish states of full quantifiability from states of mixed quantifiability, in which the system also has experience. Mathematics could thereby provide a signpost for qualia without reducing their intrinsic characters to quantities. The proposed correspondence paints an ontological triptych: nothing : zero :: physical thing : value :: quale : singularity. The paper identifies a leading candidate for the form the failure takes--a loop of comparisons, each of which can be satisfied, that cannot all be satisfied together--and considers what would establish its realization in the brain and other systems. The paper also considers implications for artificial consciousness.

title: Formally-Verifiable and Human-Interpretable RTL Generation with LLM-Guided Stepwise Refinement
ss_tldr: This work presents a framework for LLM-guided, correct-by-construction RTL generation that combines the generative capabilities of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of stepwise refinement, laying the foundation for self-improving hardware generation.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are accelerating register-transfer level (RTL) development, but ensuring the correctness of generated designs remains a major challenge. Existing LLM-driven workflows rely heavily on simulation-based verification, which provides limited correctness guarantees, and often offer little insight into the design decisions behind the generated RTL. We present a framework for LLM-guided, correct-by-construction RTL generation that combines the generative capabilities of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of stepwise refinement. The framework translates natural-language requirements into a formal hardware contract and progressively refines the contract into an implementation. At each refinement step, the LLM proposes a design decision, while the refinement engine applies the corresponding transformation only after formally verifying its correctness. The resulting program is formally verified against the contract and then translated into synthesizable RTL. The recorded derivation allows every line of generated RTL to be traced back to the design decisions and requirements that motivated it. Beyond generating verified implementations, the framework provides reliable verification feedback and reusable design experience, laying the foundation for self-improving hardware generation.

title: Dual-Branch Gated Fusion for Open-Set Audio Deepfake Source Tracing
ss_tldr: This work proposes a dual-branch gated fusion framework that pairs XLSR-53 with CORES, a 66-dimensional descriptor that, unlike prior Linear Filter Bank (LFB)-only work, spans cepstral, oscillatory, rhythmic, energy, and spectral dimensions to capture complementary synthesis artifacts.
abstract: Attributing a synthetic utterance to its originating system remains an open challenge: closed-set models fail to reject unseen synthesizers and produce overconfident predictions. To address this, we propose a dual-branch gated fusion framework that pairs XLSR-53 with CORES, a 66-dimensional descriptor that, unlike prior Linear Filter Bank (LFB)-only work, spans cepstral, oscillatory, rhythmic, energy, and spectral dimensions to capture complementary synthesis artifacts. Our analysis shows XLSR-53 remains discriminative in-domain (ID) while CORES generalizes stably under distribution shift (OOD), yet their naive concatenation fails due to SSL representational imbalance. To resolve this, an input-conditioned gate adaptively weights each branch under joint training with cross-entropy, an energy margin loss for ID/OOD separation, and a gate diversity term. On the MLAAD benchmark, our system achieves 97.6\% ID accuracy, 4.9\% EERc, and an 83.5\% relative FPR95 reduction over the Interspeech 2025 baseline.

title: Which Modality Decides? Counterfactual Modality Attribution for Multimodal Classifiers
ss_tldr: This work introduces Counterfactual Modality Attribution (CMA), which connects modality-level contributions to explicit prediction-changing edits and enables predictions to be screened by modality reliance and investigated through explicit counterfactual edits.
abstract: Multimodal classifiers can achieve high accuracy while exploiting modality-specific shortcuts. Modality attribution quantifies the contributions of image and text, but does not by itself identify which input changes would alter a suspicious prediction. We introduce Counterfactual Modality Attribution (CMA), which connects modality-level contributions to explicit prediction-changing edits. CMA uses image and text diffusion priors to generate counterfactual references and constructs a two-player reference game whose Shapley--Taylor decomposition separates image, text, and interaction contributions. The method requires class-score queries but no model gradients. Attribution profiles are compared with a reference population to prioritize predictions with atypical modality reliance for review, while counterfactual edits expose localized evidence for inspection. On controlled image- and text-biased classifiers, CMA identifies the ground truth dominant modality for all evaluated inputs. On planted-shortcut benchmarks, it achieves shortcut-reliance detection AUROCs of 0.987 on Synthetic MNIST and 1.000 on OpenI, with image-shortcut localization IoUs of 0.97 and 0.84, respectively. An API experiment demonstrates applicability to a native multimodal language model with scored answer choices. CMA enables predictions to be screened by modality reliance and investigated through explicit counterfactual edits.

title: Smooth Inliers, Erratic Outliers: Frequency-Aware Mamba for Two-View Correspondence Learning
ss_tldr: SFMambaNet is proposed, which scans the matches cluster by cluster, so that correct matches vary slowly along the sequence while wrong ones stay erratic, and filters the scans with learnable frequency-domain gates between its forward and backward passes, showing that frequency is a natural language for describing agreement between correspondences.
abstract: When shown matches between two photographs of the same cathedral, people can tell at a glance which ones are wrong: a window matched to its look-alike jumps against its neighbors, while correct matches shift together. Two-view correspondence learning, also called correspondence pruning, asks a network to make this judgment for thousands of candidate matches, most of which are wrong. Mamba, a fast sequence model, now drives strong pruners, but it reads the matches as a plain sequence, and whether its scan can capture such agreement is unclear. We propose SFMambaNet, which scans the matches cluster by cluster, so that correct matches vary slowly along the sequence while wrong ones stay erratic, and filters the scanned features with learnable frequency-domain gates between its forward and backward passes. On camera pose estimation, outlier removal and homography estimation, we find that SFMambaNet outperforms spatial-domain Mamba baselines with about two million parameters. Contrary to the usual expectation that such gains come from extra capacity, we find that a parameter-free low-pass filter beats point-wise layers as large as the gates. The learned gates turn low-pass on their own and make the scan far less sensitive to how the matches are shuffled. Together, these results show that frequency is a natural language for describing agreement between correspondences, with implications for other sequence models that must read unordered sets, such as point clouds and graphs.

title: EEG-FM-Audit: A Systematic Evaluation and Analysis Pipeline for EEG Foundation Models
ss_tldr: Extensive experiments reveal that well-tuned supervised baselines can match or outperform tuned FMs in some cases, despite requiring significantly fewer parameters, and ablation analysis indicates that FM pre-training is indispensable for data-scarce downstream tasks, whereas the contribution of pre-trained linguistic components depends heavily on model architecture.
abstract: EEG foundation models (EEG-FMs) show potential for learning generalized representations from heterogeneous EEG signals. However, existing studies exhibit three critical limitations: opaque model tuning, unverified contributions of complex learning paradigms to EEG-FMs, and a limited understanding of the neurophysiological features that FMs rely on to make decisions. To address these challenges, we propose EEG-FM-Audit, a systematic evaluation and diagnostic pipeline comprising three modules: (1) a fairness-calibrated benchmarking protocol ensuring fair comparisons through model-tailored hyperparameter optimization for EEG-FMs and supervised baselines; (2) three paradigm-level ablation workflows isolating contributions of heterogeneous data scale, self-supervised pretraining, and pretrained linguistic priors; and (3) a neurophysiological probing (NPP) framework exploring whether FMs leverage valid EEG features. Extensive experiments across four leading EEG-FMs and five supervised models on four datasets reveal that well-tuned supervised baselines can match or outperform tuned FMs in some cases, despite requiring significantly fewer parameters. Furthermore, ablation analysis indicates that FM pre-training is indispensable for data-scarce downstream tasks, whereas the contribution of pre-trained linguistic components depends heavily on model architecture. Finally, NPP analysis shows that FMs generally extract the established temporal, spatial, and spectral characteristics of the evaluated datasets, establishing a systematic diagnostic benchmark for assessing EEG-FMs.

title: Learning response-aware patient dynamics for respiratory support
ss_tldr: A response-aware patient dynamics model that explicitly represents physiological change during autoregressive state updating is proposed that achieves comparable overall trajectory prediction to patient dynamics baselines, with more consistent improvements when physiological states are changing.
abstract: Respiratory support can shape the short-term physiological trajectory of critically ill patients, but patients receiving the same intervention may follow different physiological trajectories. Clinical patient dynamics models typically predict future states from recent physiology and recorded interventions, while physiological change is mainly represented through the predicted future state. We propose a response-aware patient dynamics model that explicitly represents physiological change during autoregressive state updating. The model decomposes predicted physiological change into state-dependent baseline dynamics and respiratory-support-associated deviations, with room air providing a reference for the decomposition. We provide a formal analysis of this reference-anchored formulation. A response pathway encodes the predicted physiological change and uses it to update the latent patient state across the forecast horizon. Across ICU cohorts from two independent institutions, the proposed model achieves comparable overall trajectory prediction to patient dynamics baselines, with more consistent improvements when physiological states are changing.

title: PATH-Bench: Path-Dependent Evaluation of Lifelong Agents
abstract: Lifelong LLM agents increasingly adapt through external learning states that store past interactions as retrievable memories or reusable skills, yet existing benchmarks rarely account for how the path of accumulated experience shapes what agents transfer and retain. In this work, we establish PATH-Bench, a benchmark for path-dependent evaluation of lifelong agents. PATH-Bench estimates directed task relationships via multi-model in-context learning, constructs probe-centered sequences with controlled helpful and interfering histories, and repeatedly evaluates probe tasks to measure average performance, forward transfer, backward transfer, and forgetting. We evaluate eight representative agents on single-turn code generation and multi-turn tool-use tasks under positive- and negative-dominant histories. Benchmark results show that experience utility depends jointly on how experience is represented and on the task's interaction structure, that strong transfer does not ensure retention, and that later experience can reshape gains acquired earlier in the learning path. Based on these findings, we propose Selective Experience Use (SEU), an agent harness that regulates how path-accumulated experience influences each new task, admitting helpful items while filtering out potential interference. SEU consistently reduces forgetting while improving forward transfer in the majority of settings. The PATH-Bench provides both a controlled evaluation framework and actionable guidance for designing more selective and robust lifelong agents. The benchmark data and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/Xidong-Yang/Pathbench.

title: How Many Counterfactuals Does It Take? Probing VLM Hallucinations Through Circuits and Causal Effects
ss_tldr: The sample complexity of counterfactual robustness for hallucinated outputs in VLMs is studied and empirical bounds on the minimum number of counterfactual samples required to reliably detect instability in hallucinated outputs are derived.
abstract: Visual Language Models (VLMs) are known to produce hallucinated predictions that are not grounded in visual evidence, yet existing approaches lack a principled understanding of how robust such predictions are under counterfactual perturbations. In this work, we study the sample complexity of counterfactual robustness for hallucinated outputs in VLMs. We define a causal influence metric based on log-probability differences between factual, counterfactual, and activation-patched runs, and use it to characterize the stability of hallucinated predictions. By leveraging circuit discovery techniques (CD-T), we identify model components responsible for these predictions and track their activation differences across counterfactual samples. We then derive empirical bounds on the minimum number of counterfactual samples m required to reliably detect instability in hallucinated outputs, using concentration inequalities and variance estimates of the causal influence distribution.

title: WorldCrafter: Consistent Video World Model with Implicit 3D-aware Memory
ss_tldr: WorldCrafter is a video world model that learns a camera-queryable implicit 3D-aware memory that enables streaming scene exploration from a single input image or text prompt and shows substantial gains in long-horizon consistency and camera-control accuracy while preserving visual quality during minute-scale exploration.
abstract: Video world models enable interactive exploration of dynamic environments, yet struggle to respect prior observations over long horizons and across viewpoints. We present WorldCrafter, a video world model that learns a camera-queryable implicit 3D-aware memory for this purpose. The key insight is to let the requested viewpoint shape how multi-view evidence is compressed into the video generator's limited token budget. Trained jointly with the video generator, a memory encoder and pose-conditioned readout module integrate historical observations into a fixed set of target view-specific tokens before denoising, without explicit depth-based correspondences. By combining this memory with recent temporal context and few-step distillation, WorldCrafter enables streaming scene exploration from a single input image or text prompt. Experiments across static and dynamic scenes show substantial gains in long-horizon consistency and camera-control accuracy while preserving visual quality during minute-scale exploration.

title: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy Large Language Models, Agentic AI, and Multimodal Systems
ss_tldr: A unified framework that connects output-level, trajectory-level, and cross-modal assessment through eight trustworthiness dimensions, providing a structured basis for assessing both system performance and the credibility of the evidence supporting it, with empirical validation across deployment contexts remaining an essential next step.
abstract: Benchmark scores alone provide an incomplete basis for assessing the trustworthiness of modern artificial intelligence systems. Large language models (LLMs), agentic systems, and multimodal models (MLLMs) require different forms of assessment, yet their evaluation evidence must remain interpretable for development and oversight. We propose a unified framework that connects output-level, trajectory-level, and cross-modal assessment through eight trustworthiness dimensions: capability, robustness, safety, fairness, transparency, governance, oversight, and efficiency. The framework preserves system-specific metrics while mapping native measurements to common performance bands, accompanied by uncertainty estimates and traceable evidence. A meta-evaluation layer examines the validity, reliability, and reproducibility of the evaluation itself. Multidimensional profiles expose strengths and weaknesses, while safety-critical overrides prevent aggregate scores from masking critical failures. Mappings to governance frameworks, international standards, and European Union regulatory requirements connect technical assessment with oversight needs. The framework provides a structured basis for assessing both system performance and the credibility of the evidence supporting it, with empirical validation across deployment contexts remaining an essential next step.

title: Selective-Rerouter: A Rerouting Strategy for Hypothetical Post-Disaster Urban Scenarios with a Thin-Boundary Co-Simulator
ss_tldr: This work proposes Selective-Rerouter, a delayed-binding anonymous rerouting strategy for partitioned environments under a thin-boundary information-isolation constraint, and builds a SUMO-based co-simulator coupling Selective-Rerouter on the intact side with a fixed DTN-UAV Forwarder inside each damaged corner.
abstract: Hypothetical post-disaster urban environments may be partitioned into disjoint delay-tolerant-network (DTN) subregions under a thin-boundary information-isolation constraint, which severely limits cross-zone message delivery and makes centralized rerouting impractical. To address this, we propose Selective-Rerouter, a delayed-binding anonymous rerouting strategy for such partitioned environments. The scheme jointly exploits road occupancy and traffic speed for bottleneck detection, adaptively enlarges its upstream intervention window with congestion severity to include vehicles imminently approaching bottlenecks, and evaluates paths via horizon-aware fusion of live measurements and short-term forecasts, where only the prediction head of LSTAN-GERPE is fine-tuned with a path-ranking loss to preserve travel-time ordering, while a driver-aware scaling factor adjusts forecasts without altering live observations. Vehicles reroute only upon bottleneck encounters and keep K candidate routes. To assess performance under information isolation, we build a SUMO-based co-simulator coupling Selective-Rerouter on the intact side with a fixed DTN-UAV Forwarder inside each damaged corner. The forwarder consumes only scalar cost-announcements, performs no path-cost computation, and resolves civilian identities solely after bundles reach gateway buffers, thus acting as a testbed component rather than a novel DTN routing algorithm. Evaluations include standalone validation over undamaged districts, corner-level verification of cost-announcement-compliant bundle handoff, and four-corner tests that replace only the intact-side rerouting policy. Results show that hybrid live-forecast costing yields dominant travel-time gains. All experiments use discrete SUMO runs based on real-world urban road topology with artificially injected network partition damage, with no physical prototype.

title: When Simpler Is Better: Evaluating Translation Pipelines for Medieval Latin Manuscripts
ss_tldr: A systematic framework for evaluating the full image-to-translation pipeline on medieval Latin manuscripts, a setting in which scribal shorthand, ligatures, and parchment degradation expose failure modes that are invisible in clean-text benchmarks, and introduces the Interpres-Parallel-Corpus (IPC), a novel dataset to be the first of its kind for medieval Latin.
abstract: Despite remarkable progress in machine translation, Vision Language Models (VLMs) struggle on historical manuscripts, a domain that stresses core Natural Language Processing (NLP) capabilities: low-resource transliteration, archaic vocabulary, and noisy input signals. We present a systematic framework for evaluating the full image-to-translation pipeline on medieval Latin manuscripts, a setting in which scribal shorthand, ligatures, and parchment degradation expose failure modes that are invisible in clean-text benchmarks. Benchmarking on the CATMuS Latin dataset reveals a specialization gap: domain-specific Optical Character Recognition (OCR) models reduce character error rate by up to 4.3$\times$ compared to general-purpose VLMs, despite operating at orders of magnitude fewer parameters. We introduce the Interpres-Parallel-Corpus (IPC), a novel dataset comprising 1,383 aligned manuscript image lines, transcriptions, and expert translations, to our knowledge the first of its kind for medieval Latin. Our experiments uncover a complexity paradox: the simplest pipeline, a specialized OCR model feeding directly into a VLM, outperforms all multi-component variants. Adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or post-OCR correction introduces prompt saturation and error propagation that degrade aggregate translation quality. These findings offer both a new benchmark and practical guidance for deploying translation systems in low-resource historical settings.

title: LCSHBench: A Multilingual, Consensus-Grounded Benchmark for Library of Congress Subject Heading Assignment
ss_tldr: This work introduces LCSHBench, a low-rank fine-tune of a 300M on-device embedder that improves cross-lingual retrieval and beats a 3,072-dimensional hosted embedder on development exact recall@200 and beats a 3,072-dimensional hosted embedder on development exact recall@200.
abstract: Automated subject cataloging assigns controlledvocabulary headings to bibliographic records, but LCSH has no standard public benchmark. We introduce LCSHBench: 22,346 books in 15 languages from the openly licensed Harvard, Columbia, and Princeton catalogs. Records enter only when at least two independent cataloging agencies assigned LCSH; we release per-catalog provenance plus union and unanimous answer views. A concordance study of 465,187 works cataloged by all three libraries shows why this design matters: libraries usually agree on the underlying topic (93.3% share a concept-level heading) but often differ in exact expression (39.4% have identical heading sets). LCSHBench therefore scores both exact and concept matches, with set and rank metrics broken down by language and heading type, across open-vocabulary generation and full-vocabulary retrieval. As a first demonstration, a low-rank fine-tune of a 300M on-device embedder improves cross-lingual retrieval and beats a 3,072-dimensional hosted embedder on development exact recall@200 (0.659 vs 0.623). The language panel shows the gain is not uniform, and held-out-test and end-to-end confirmation remain future work.

title: ArgGYM: A Procedural, Engine-Verified Benchmark for Structured Defeasible Reasoning
ss_tldr: ArgGYM is introduced, a procedural benchmark and RLVR-compatible training environment for structured defeasible reasoning that decomposes this reasoning into twelve tasks and grounds task-specific scoring in a symbolic argumentation engine that computes the formal states used to evaluate model outputs.
abstract: Recent progress in large language model reasoning has been driven by benchmarks and reinforcement learning environments with automatically verifiable rewards, particularly in mathematics, code, and formal logic. These settings make model accuracy easier to evaluate and optimize, but it remains unclear how far success under fixed problem specifications and stable evaluation criteria transfers to reasoning outside such domains. Real-world reasoning often proceeds under incomplete and revisable information: conclusions may be supported provisionally, defeated by counter-evidence, reinstated by further arguments, or revised when stronger reasons become available. Reasoning of this kind is generally referred to as defeasible reasoning. We introduce ArgGYM, a procedural benchmark and RLVR-compatible training environment for structured defeasible reasoning. ArgGYM decomposes this reasoning into twelve tasks and grounds task-specific scoring in a symbolic argumentation engine that computes the formal states used to evaluate model outputs. It includes a frozen benchmark of 1,440 verified instances across fifteen curriculum configurations, two argument preference orderings, and two set orderings, while the same generators and verifiers can produce fresh instances, reducing dependence on static test sets, for both evaluation and verifiable-reward training. On the frozen benchmark, frontier and open-weight models show sharply different reasoning profiles: they can recover substantial parts of structured answers without solving the complete task, and performance declines in later curriculum configurations with longer dependencies and more interacting structures. Training Qwen3.5-4B with ArgGYM's verifiers as rewards more than doubles complete-task success on held-out instances, with the largest gains on constructive tasks.

title: Looking Is Not Picking: An Attention-Segment Account of Tool-Selection Failures in LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents mis-call tools, and the natural guess is that the model failed to see the right tool in a crowded harness. We show the opposite through a lens concurrent work sets aside -- the model's attention to labeled tool-definition segments. On real BFCL failures, by per-candidate attention argmax the model attends most to the correct tool 80% of the time (vs. 21% chance), and the gold is the under-attended segment on only 10%: it looks at the right tool and still picks wrong. This directly refutes the intuitive "crowded-harness / lost-in-the-middle" explanation: the failure is at the decision readout, not the harness, and we pin it there three ways. (1) Input vs. readout: repairing the prompt (reordering or duplicating the gold tool) recovers <=23% of failures, while readout-side interventions recover 59-91%. (2) Representation-invariance: two gold-pointed interventions in different representations -- an additive attention-logit bias and a residual-stream steering vector -- recover largely the same failures (per-task Jaccard 0.865 pooled, 0.79-0.91 per model), so the bottleneck is localized to the readout independent of which representation is poked. (3) A training-free, gold-free selector: per-segment attention closes most of the gold-free-vs-oracle gap on BFCL (+11.9 pts pooled function-name selection vs. +17.9-pt oracle headroom) and adds +14.9 pts on Seal-Tools; every model positive (exact McNemar p<=8e-4 each). Scopes differ: the causal attention-bias dose-response is bidirectional and monotonic on 10 mask-honoring models (3-32B), the full 0.5-32B span carrying only the correlational diagnostic; the deployable selector is evaluated on 5 single-turn models and does not yet transfer to a multi-turn loop.

title: Auto-Policy, not Auto-Skill: Compiled Agent Skills for the Physical World
ss_tldr: Edge Skillguard is proposed, a typed invocation policy co-versioned with the actuator-owning Skill and enforced at the message boundary by a deterministic, fail-closed evaluator over leases, world state, and sensor freshness.
abstract: Self-evolving Skill harnesses automatically rewrite an agent's procedural knowledge to improve efficiency, yet leave execution authority unconstrained. A Skill specifies how an agent should act, whereas a policy decides which requests may become physical actions; current Skill formats package procedure as markdown and scripts and leave authorization to the model. This gap is critical when a wrong invocation unlocks a door. We term the resulting failure Borrowed Authority: an inter-agent message pairs an instruction with an unverifiable permission claim, and the receiving Skill has no typed way to reject it. Across six open-weight receiver configurations (9,510 episodes), models execute 87% of unauthorized requests with no rule, 91% under a one-line rule, 25% when given the full policy in prose and a state-reading tool, and 18% behind a dedicated LLM checker. Failures concentrate on near misses (case variants, whitespace, wildcards, or just-expired readings), and where bare commands hesitate, an unverified claim displaces state checks. We propose Edge Skillguard, a typed invocation policy co-versioned with the actuator-owning Skill and enforced at the message boundary by a deterministic, fail-closed evaluator over leases, world state, and sensor freshness. Rather than using models as runtime filters, Edge Skillguard compiles prose rules offline behind an admission and operator-lattice tightening gate: across all six configurations and five policies, gated compilation yields verified guards (28/30 zero-shot, 30/30 after one feedback turn) and blocks 12/12 model-generated loosenings. On an edge testbed, Edge Skillguard admits 0/682 generated violations and 150/150 authorized requests at about 1 ms per decision, keeping invocation policy a fixed point outside the evolving harness's reach. Code and data: https://github.com/zhonghaozhan/edge-skillguard

title: Competing at Every Price Point with Agentic Evolution over a Menu of LLMs
ss_tldr: This paper shows a path to multi-LLM Python agents with Pareto domination of both the top-scoring and the lowest-cost competing points by evolving multi-LLM Python agents from training pools of at most 100 examples.
abstract: Consider a firm that surveys its competition for a particular agentic task and seeks to offer superior accuracy at every price point. A firm that Pareto-dominated its competitors would leave no rational customer a reason to buy elsewhere. This paper shows a path to this kind of capability by evolving multi-LLM Python agents from training pools of at most 100 examples. Given a priced menu of nine LLM endpoints; brief documentation of the task, objective, and API; a simple seed agent; and an operator-chosen per-problem cost target--usually set at an incumbent's own price--RoboPhD, an evolutionary meta-agent, evolves complete agent programs that attack the public frontiers of two semantically dissimilar tasks point by point: DS-1000 (execution-checked code generation) and PaperFindingBench (LLM-judged scientific document retrieval). On public leaderboards for each task, the evolved agents hold every Pareto-frontier slot on PaperFindingBench and all but one on DS-1000, including Pareto domination of both the top-scoring and the lowest-cost competing points.

title: Does Regime-Gated Attention Help Stock Return Prediction? A Leakage-Controlled, Pre-Registered Evaluation
ss_tldr: The Adaptive Financial Transformer is re-examine, which biases self-attention with feature-group similarities weighted by gates that a market-regime encoder produces, and is statistically indistinguishable from a vanilla Transformer and less stable than gradient boosting or ridge regression.
abstract: Regime-aware attention is an appealing inductive bias for stock-return prediction, but claims about it are rarely tested under leakage-controlled, out-of-sample conditions. We re-examine the Adaptive Financial Transformer (AFT), which biases self-attention with feature-group similarities weighted by gates that a market-regime encoder produces. First, on a single stock under a corrected protocol (aligned and purged windows, identical test dates for all models, cost-aware non-overlapping backtests, five seeds, Diebold-Mariano tests), no learned model beats the historical-mean forecast. The AFT's regime and context components are numerically inert: the learned gates have 0.9982 of maximal entropy, the context bias has 0.020 of the scale of the attention logits, and we show that the product of two simplex-normalised weightings attenuates it by a factor 1/G. Removing these components changes nothing. Second, we build a point-in-time S&P 500 panel (500 stocks, 1,390,254 stock-days) with 63 stationary features whose causality is verified exactly, and evaluate a model zoo and a layered meta-model with yearly walk-forward refits, a development period (2016-2022) and a sealed, pre-registered holdout (2023-2025). Cross-sectional breadth turns weak signals into detectable ones; the AFT is statistically indistinguishable from a vanilla Transformer and less stable than gradient boosting or ridge regression; six learned meta-learners fail to beat an equal-weight rank combination; and a hysteresis rule roughly halves turnover. On the holdout, the pre-registered primary system (21-day horizon) fails (rank IC 0.0003, one-sided p=0.49), whereas the same system at a 5-day horizon, a pre-registered secondary result, attains a rank IC of 0.0172 (one-sided p=0.038) and a net long-short Sharpe ratio of 0.34 at 5 bp per side. Code: https://github.com/Dishan18/FinancialTransformer

title: VERITAS: Verifier-Guided Proof Search for Zero-Shot Formal Theorem Proving
ss_tldr: VERITAS is a zero-shot framework that feeds what Lean reports (error messages with their position, verified partial proofs, and remaining goals) back into proof search, and solves more theorems than three re-implemented feedback baselines at a third to a half of their search cost.
abstract: LLM-based formal provers often collapse the verifier's output into a pass/fail bit. We present VERITAS, a zero-shot framework that feeds what Lean reports (error messages with their position, verified partial proofs, and remaining goals) back into proof search. Phase 1 samples N whole proofs; Phase 2 searches a tree of verified partial proofs with a Tactician, automated step repair, a Critic that ranks states and allocates the budget, and a Retriever. On miniF2F test, VERITAS solves 86.9% with Claude Haiku 5.5 and 82.8% with GPT-6 Luna, against 71.7% and 61.1% for Best-of-5 sampling, and solves more theorems than three re-implemented feedback baselines at a third to a half of their search cost. We also evaluate on 55 combinatorics problems of CombiBench and release code and run logs at https://github.com/CoderDoge1108/VERITAS.

title: A Theory on Flow Matching with Neural Networks
ss_tldr: This work establishes convergence guarantees for gradient descent in the over-parameterized 2-layered ReLU neural network regime and derives generalization bounds for the conditional velocity-field matching objective.
abstract: In this work, we develop theoretical foundation for flow matching with neural-network-parameterized conditional velocity fields. We establish convergence guarantees for gradient descent in the over-parameterized 2-layered ReLU neural network regime. We derive generalization bounds for the conditional velocity-field matching objective. Building on these results, we provide Wasserstein-distance guarantees for the samples generated by the induced flow. Our analysis is based on generalization bound for multi-task representation learning with unbounded losses, which may be of independent interest beyond flow-based generative modeling. These theoretical results are validated through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world image benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/qishuoyin/FlowMatchNN.

title: OpenRFM: Democratizing Frontier Predictive Intelligence on Relational Data
ss_tldr: OpenRFM is an open recipe for building an RFM from synthetic databases alone, whose data generator, model and training code are all open and achieves the best mean rank on 32 benchmark tasks.
abstract: Relational databases hold most enterprise data, and predicting on them has long required hand-written feature joins and a model trained for each task. Relational foundation models (RFMs) remove this per-task engineering by predicting on an unseen database from a few labelled examples in one forward pass. However, the strongest RFMs are closed, and open RFMs pre-trained on synthetic data lag far behind. Prior work attributes this gap to the lack of real pre-training data. We find that much of this gap comes from an incomplete synthetic prior and from a sparse context. Existing synthetic priors lack history-dependent labels, so models pre-trained on them do not learn the temporal and relational dynamics behind real tasks. A bounded context also often misses the evidence that a task needs. We present OpenRFM, an open recipe for building an RFM from synthetic databases alone, whose data generator, model and training code are all open. OpenRFM has three components. (1) A relational adapter, pre-trained on synthetic event streams with history-dependent labels, encodes the sampled context of each entity into a feature row and performs in-context learning along the relation axis, over the history of the entity and its related entities. (2) A frozen tabular foundation model predicts from labelled support rows and performs in-context learning along the batch axis. (3) An optional harness, which an LLM agent builds for each task, rewrites the schema so that the evidence a task needs enters the bounded context. On 32 benchmark tasks, OpenRFM achieves the best mean rank, 3.00 against 3.63 for RelAgent and 5.34 for KumoRFM-2. The code is available at https://github.com/Quant-Spirit/openrfm.

title: Feature Lottery? A Bifurcation Theory of Concept Emergence
ss_tldr: A bifurcation theory of representation dynamics is introduced to detect the onset of usable structure, the crystallization of feature identities, and the beginning of representation collapse many epochs before downstream metrics react.
abstract: Neural networks learn structured representations at specific points during training, yet pinpointing these transitions usually requires post-hoc, label-dependent metrics. We introduce a bifurcation theory of representation dynamics to detect these moments in real time. By analyzing a passive GMM probe on an evolving encoder, we show that the emergence of structure corresponds to a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation driven by the loss Hessian. Comparing a theoretically predictable zero-crossing ($β_c$) with the network's current state ($β$) yields a dynamic ratio, $β(t)/β_c(t)$. Computed solely from hidden states, this ratio is a universal, label-free phase coordinate for representation dynamics. We validate the four transition regimes this coordinate predicts across diverse settings: sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on language models (Pythia), self-supervised learning (CIFAR), and grokking (modular arithmetic). Crucially, under finite dissipation, macroscopic symmetry breaking can lag the initial zero-crossing by orders of magnitude, providing a rigorous dynamical explanation for delayed generalization in grokking. Microscopically, the theory predicts that the bifurcation creates a shared unstable subspace that forces collective symmetry breaking. We call this the \emph{feature lottery} in SAE training: a feature's eventual interpretability is determined very early on. Just $5\%$ into training, early atom purity strongly predicts final purity at convergence: atoms in the top $10\%$ at the $5\%$ mark reach a final POS purity of $0.82$, versus $0.47$ for the bottom $10\%$ and $0.22$ for chance.
